head_commit.message:
## New Features
- Added persistent goal workflows with `/goal`, goal status indicators, pause/unpause/clear controls, and runtime continuation for long-running objectives (#18073, #18074, #18075, #18076, #18077).
- Added configurable TUI key bindings through `[tui.keymap]`, with shortcut hints reflecting the resolved config (#18593).
- Added a top-level `codex update` command that runs the detected package-manager update path directly (#19933).
- Expanded `/plugins` with marketplace installation, cached remote plugin bundles, remote uninstall support, and plugin-bundled hooks (#18704, #19456, #19705, #19914).
- Added external-agent migration for recent sessions plus MCP servers, hooks, commands, and subagents (#19895, #19949).
- Improved MultiAgentV2 configuration with feature-scoped thread caps, root/subagent context hints, configurable wait minimums, and nested spawn behavior independent of legacy depth limits (#19792, #19805, #20052, #20180).

## Bug Fixes
- Fixed `turn/interrupt` hanging when the target turn had already completed (#18392).
- Thread resume now preserves the original model provider, handles large remote resume responses, and moves local cwd filtering into `thread/list` for faster resume/fork menus (#19287, #19920, #19931).
- TUI scrollback now reflows after terminal resize, slash-command columns stay stable, shell mode exits cleanly with `Esc`, and keyboard reporting is reset on exit (#18575, #19511, #19625, #19986).
- Bedrock GPT-5.4 now uses compatible apply-patch tooling, valid reasoning levels, and the current Mantle endpoint/model IDs (#19416, #19461, #20109).
- Hardened managed network and sandbox boundaries around proxy bypasses, resolved connect targets, IPv6 scopes, Linux bridge helpers, Windows elevated pipes, and `git -C` approval checks (#19283, #19995, #19999, #20001, #20002, #20085).
- Delegated patch approvals now show the proposed diff preview consistently with main-thread approvals (#19709).

## Documentation
- Refreshed the bundled OpenAI Docs skill for GPT-5.5 guidance, GPT-image-2, and clearer prompting/upgrade recommendations (#19407, #19422, #19443).
- Updated app-server docs for WebSocket-over-Unix-socket transport, remote plugin uninstall, remote-control status/overrides, and provider capability reads (#19244, #19456, #19919, #20047, #20049).
- Documented config support for suppressing tool suggestions for specific tools, connectors, or plugins (#20072).

## Chores
- Release packaging now publishes dedicated `codex-app-server` artifacts and intentionally ships Linux release assets as MUSL-only (#19445, #19447).
- The Python app-server SDK is publishable as `openai-codex-app-server-sdk` with runtime dependencies pinned to the Codex release version (#18996).
- Memory code was split out of `codex-core`; background memory startup now waits for real user turns and backs off when rate limits are low (#19818, #19860, #19970, #19990).
- Deprecated `--full-auto`, removing it from the TUI path while keeping a warning period for `codex exec` users (#20133).
- Removed the obsolete `js_repl` feature and related docs/build wiring (#19410).

## Changelog

workflow_runs.name: Bazel
workflow_runs.display_title: Fallback login callback port when default is busy (#19334)

head_commit.message:
Fallback login callback port when default is busy (#19334)

## Summary
- Keep the preferred ChatGPT login callback port `1455` first.
- Preserve the existing `/cancel` recovery for stale Codex login
servers.
- Fall back to the registered localhost callback port `1457` when `1455`
remains unavailable.

## Why
Cursor and Codex Desktop both use the ChatGPT account login callback
server. On Windows, Cursor can already be listening on `127.0.0.1:1455`
/ `[::1]:1455`, causing Codex Desktop sign-in to fail with:

`Local callback port 1455 is already in use on this machine.`

Codex already attempted to cancel a stale Codex login server on that
port, but if the listener does not release the port, the old behavior
was to fail. The new behavior falls back to `1457`, which matches the
fixed redirect URI being registered server-side in
`openai/openai#863817`. This keeps the OAuth `redirect_uri` inside
Hydra's exact allow-list instead of choosing an arbitrary ephemeral
port.

## Validation
- `just fmt`
- `cargo test -p codex-login`
- `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`
